summary: Most earnings noise cleared overnight: AAPL, CLX, MTCH, CALX, IDXX and ULS have all reported, and the next dated cluster is Thursday 11-05 (CARG held, plus TPR, RL, DBX, ONC), with SMG tomorrow. Macro event risk is concentrated today: midterms, the tech/AI-capex selloff (AAPL about -4% premarket despite a beat), and crypto still digesting the Binance hack with Block reporting after the close and Circle before the open on 11-04. Two items are unverified: CVS may not have reported yet (a 11-03 Benzinga preview says 'ahead of Q3 earnings'), and the Cheniere 8-K 1.01 filed today is unread.

event_risk.why: Held. Company-confirmed Q3 results 11-05 after the close (per earlier runs; the file estimate also says 11-05), 2 trading days out. The thesis invalidates on a negative surprise inside five trading days, so the clause is live (L5). No filings or headlines in the window.

Held. Binance hack aftermath is moving from crisis to cleanup: withdrawals resume in phases (next phase Tuesday), 98% of users stayed, North Korea denies the US attribution, the Secret Service is investigating. On the news alone the 'exchange failure' invalidation clause has not tripped (L5): Binance is reopening and repaying, not failing. Live dated risks: midterms today (an analyst warns of a post-midterm correction), Block earnings after the close today, Circle earnings 11-04 before the open, MSCI/Strategy index decision 11-11. Headlines had BTC below $77k on 11-02 with ETF outflows and $226M of liquidations, and bears cite $73k. The price stop is a PM matter, but headline price is near the level the learning file cites.

Fiscal Q4 results 11-04 (company-confirmed per earlier runs; the file estimate agrees), 1 trading day out. Wells Fargo raised its PT to $71 from $60 (Overweight) on 11-02. The 10-16 8-K 5.02 was never read and has aged out, so management-change risk stays unverified.

Earnings 11-05 (company-announced per earlier runs), 2 trading days out. Four PT cuts last week (UBS, Jefferies, Baird, Wells Fargo) with ratings held; nothing new in this window, so the drift flag is unresolved.

Midterms today and the AI-capex selloff is still running: Apple about -4% premarket on memory-cost margin warnings, Tom Lee calling a bottom while saying buyers wait until after the midterms, Elliott hedging for a bear market, Howard Marks questioning AI valuations. Futures are mixed on Trump's Iran settlement hopes (oil fell about 7% on 11-02). Seasonal counterweight: S&P up in 19 of 19 midterm Nov-April windows. A QQQ-tagged Questcorp copper-mine item is a mis-tag.

Two new items. An 8-K 1.01/7.01 was filed today; the item numbers do not say what it is, and the likeliest match is documentation for the $1.2B senior notes due 2037 priced today (refinancing), but that is an inference and not read. Separately, a TradingView/fiscal.ai note says Sabine Pass gas intake dropped and two of six liquefaction trains may be offline (data-inferred, unconfirmed). Earnings passed 10-29.

Unverified, and earlier notes may have been wrong. The file shows the next estimate as 2027-02-09 and there is no 8-K 2.02 or 10-Q, but a Benzinga piece today says CVS expects Q3 EPS $1.65 on $104.69B revenue 'ahead of Q3 earnings', which implies the quarter has not been reported. Earnings could fall inside the window. Standing negatives: the Labor Department PBM disclosure rule and the SilverScript PDP exit.

notable.headline: Apple beats Q4 and guides above consensus, but warns memory prices are 'unprecedented' and will pressure gross margin; stock about -4% premarket; PT moves split (Morgan Stanley to $350, TD Cowen to $390, Barclays to $261, Argus to $400)
notable.read: Resolves the 10-29/11-02 date question and the two-sided preview. The beat was helped by $0.05 of tariff refunds, gross margin was down ex-refunds, and the market is selling margin guidance, not the top line. Siri AI may become a paid tier. Most other AAPL-tagged items (premarket roundups, Ives, Munster, prediction markets) are noise. This is a read on the whole AI-capex and component-cost group for QQQ.

notable.headline: Bitcoin falls below $77,000 ahead of midterms; Binance resumes withdrawals in phases and replaces 90% of stolen funds; North Korea denies the hack; Block reports after the close today, Circle before the open 11-04
notable.read: Continues the 10-30 Binance flag, which has come to less than feared on price so far (BTC about flat through the weekend, then lower Monday on ETF outflows and liquidations). The exchange-failure clause has not tripped on the evidence here. Next dated risks are the midterms, the 11-04 Circle and Block prints, and the 11-11 MSCI/Strategy decision. Strategy bought 811 BTC ($65.5M) on 11-02 after its pause; Galaxy Digital and other crypto stocks fell. Prediction-market, political and price-target pieces tagged BTC are filler.

notable.read: Ends the 10-28 to 11-02 high-risk flag on the benign side: a large beat with guidance only affirmed, and the CEO handover (Garcia) landed with it. The negative preview drift (JPMorgan Underweight/$83) did not translate into a bad print.

notable.headline: KeyBanc upgrades Howmet to Overweight, PT $237
notable.read: The five post-beat PT cuts since 10-30 (BNP, Susquehanna, JPMorgan, Jefferies, BTIG) now have a counter-move. The cuts still look like valuation and rotation, not a broken thesis; an upgrade at a lower PT than the cuts' levels says the stock has fallen a long way. Cramer also named it. Unverified why.

notable.headline: Cheniere prices $1.2B senior notes due 2037; 8-K 1.01 filed today; reported disruption at Sabine Pass (two of six trains possibly offline); BMO PT to $350
notable.read: The notes are refinancing and the 1.01 probably belongs to them, but it is unread. The Sabine Pass note is data-inferred and unconfirmed, and would matter if it persists. Dividend raised to $0.625 after the 10-29 beat.

notable.read: A low-quality piece, but it contradicts the earlier assumption that CVS had already reported. It is the only dated hint; no 8-K 2.02 or results headline exists. Treat the print date as unknown and possibly near.
